articles.title: Why the rise of open source AI isn’t hurting Anthropic … yet
articles.summary: Open source models’ success isn’t coming at the expense of frontier labs. Instead, they each seem to capture two phases of the same life cycle.

articles.title: Microsoft joins AI cost-cutting trend by relying more on its own models
articles.summary: Microsoft is the latest Silicon Valley giant to cut back on its AI spending.

articles.title: Discord admits AI moderation bug wrongfully banned users over harmless images
articles.summary: The company confirmed that the issue had been affecting accounts since May, with an additional 200 users banned over the weekend before its team identified and fixed the problem.

articles.title: Claude Cowork expands to mobile and web
articles.summary: With this update, users can start a task from their desk, get status updates on their phone, and pick up the finished output later — even if their laptop is closed.

articles.summary: Forterra has deployed more than 100 of its self-driving ATVs in conflict zones in Ukraine.

articles.title: The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
articles.summary: An AI agent carried out the technical execution of a real-world ransomware attack for the first known time, but new details show a human still chose the victim, set up the infrastructure, and supplied stolen credentials — meaning it wasn't quite the fully autonomous cybercrime debut that last week's headlines suggested.

articles.title: US investors will soon get access to SK Hynix, another memory maker riding the AI boom
articles.summary: SK Hynix is experiencing a boom credited to AI. It will ride that to a multibillion-dollar U.S. IPO, expected to take place on Friday.

articles.title: If you use Google, you’re training its AI. Here’s how to opt out.
articles.summary: Consider this a belated PSA: A recent change to Google’s privacy settings is allowing the company to store more of your data, including media such as “images, files, and audio and video recordings,” to improve its AI models.

articles.title: Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 employees across Xbox, commercial sales
articles.summary: Microsoft cut around 4,800 roles, or 2.1% of its global workforce, on Monday — the latest in a series of layoffs that’s stoking fears of AI replacing jobs. The layoffs will hit Xbox and commercial sales the hardest.

articles.summary: Energy stakeholders should be focused on how to strengthen competitive markets, not abandon them, writes Todd Snitchler, president and CEO of the Electric Power Supply Association.

articles.summary: The companies said the deal marks Walmart’s first nuclear power purchase agreement and is “among the first of its kind between a large retailer and a nuclear energy facility in the United States.”

articles.summary: Maryland state agencies asked the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to end an extra 0.5% return the transmission owners earn for being PJM Interconnection members.

articles.summary: U.S. regulators and lawmakers have taken more than 350 energy affordability actions so far this year, but the problem is persistent, say researchers from the North Carolina Clean Energy Technology Center.

articles.title: APS to convert retired coal units, adding 380 MW of natural gas
articles.summary: “Given Arizona’s increasing demand for around-the-clock energy and the long timelines for adding new generation, the conversion has proven to be a viable option,” APS said.

articles.summary: Giving Advanced Power Services a waiver from the PJM Interconnection’s rules could harm other project developers, the agency said.

articles.title: Southwestern Public Service wins $113M reliability grant from Texas
articles.summary: The Texas Energy Fund has allocated more than $4 billion as part of the state’s effort to boost grid reliability. The award to SPS covers a drone-based pole inspection program and live monitoring.

articles.title: UK fusion sector poised for industrial scale-up
articles.summary: The UK fusion energy sector is entering a decisive transition from laboratory development to industrial-scale delivery, driven by rising private investment, sustained government backing, and an evolving regulatory framework designed to support deployment, speakers said at the NextGen Nuclear Summit, held in London.

articles.title: Holtec and EDF submit UK SMR project proposal
articles.summary: US-based Holtec International and France-based EDF have submitted a joint proposal for up to four SMR-300 small modular reactors at the Cottam power plant site in Nottinghamshire in the UK.

articles.title: Russia planning 'high-capacity' nuclear fuel reprocessing plant
articles.summary: Investment feasibility and site selection studies are taking place, with a decision due by the end of 2026, for a reprocessing plant for used nuclear fuel with an initial capacity of 400 tonnes per year.

articles.title: US federal loan to jumpstart AP1000 reactor supply chain
articles.summary: The US Department of Energy has conditionally committed to USD17.5 billion in loans to finance the purchase of long-lead items for up to 10 Westinghouse AP1000 reactors.

articles.title: Walmart signs nuclear power purchase agreement with Constellation
articles.summary: Retail giant Walmart has signed a long-term power purchase agreement for emissions-free electricity from Constellation's Dresden nuclear power plant in Illinois in the USA.

articles.title: AtkinsRéalis kicks off US licensing for CANDU technology
articles.summary: The sole licensee of the Canadian CANDU pressurised heavy water reactor technology has formally submitted a Notice of Intent to the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission to begin licensing it in the USA.

articles.title: Swedish state taking majority stake in Videberg Kraft
articles.summary: The Swedish government has decided that the state will take a 60% stake in Videberg Kraft AB, which plans to build three Rolls-Royce small modular reactors on the Värö Peninsula near Ringhals.

articles.title: In pictures: Work on Paks II's new units
articles.summary: Concreting work has been taking place for unit 5 at the Paks II nuclear power plant in Hungary, while earthworks on unit 6's pit are said to be proceeding on schedule, as the new government continues its review of the project.

articles.title: Canadian repository put forward for federal support
articles.summary: The project to build an underground deep geological repository system for Canada's used nuclear fuel is one of three projects of national interest put forward by ministers as candidates to be listed for support under the Building Canada Act.

articles.title: OSGE signs agreement with Włocławek for SMR plant
articles.summary: The City of Włocławek and Orlen Synthos Green Energy have signed an agreement defining the principles of cooperation in connection with the construction of up to six BWRX-300 small modular reactors in the central Polish city.

articles.title: First Lightbridge fuel samples removed from INL's Advanced Test Reactor
articles.summary: Advanced nuclear fuel developer Lightbridge Corporation has announced that the first batch of its fuel material samples have been successfully removed from Idaho National Laboratory's Advanced Test Reactor after undergoing irradiation.

articles.title: UK completes return of high-level waste to Germany
articles.summary: The third and final return of high-level waste, in the form of vitrified residue, from the UK to Germany has been completed. The waste being returned is a legacy of Sellafield's overseas fuel reprocessing programme.

articles.title: Second Taipingling unit starts up
articles.summary: Unit 2 at the Taipingling nuclear power plant has attained a sustained chain reaction for the first time, China General Nuclear announced. The unit is the second of six Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors planned for the site in Guangdong province.

articles.title: Rolls-Royce SMR plans manufacturing development centre in Derby
articles.summary: Rolls-Royce SMR has announced plans to open its Pioneer Works facility in Derby, in the East Midlands region of England. It will be its first manufacturing development centre where it will establish the build processes, precision assembly and advanced testing needed to de-risk the delivery of its small modular reactor fleet in the UK, Czech Republi

articles.title: Substation damage delaying operation of repaired Zaporizhzhia power line, says IAEA
articles.summary: After months of ceasefire negotiations, planning and complex repairs, the main external power line to Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant has been fixed - but it can’t be put back into operation because of damage to a substation 100 kilometres away, the International Atomic Energy Agency has said.

articles.title: Sogin begins re-encapsulation of uranium-thorium fuel
articles.summary: Italy's Societa Gestione Impianti Nucleari SpA has begun operations to re-encapsulate 64 uranium-thorium fuel elements currently held in the storage pool at the Itrec facility on the Rotondella site in the province of Matera, in the southern Italian region of Basilicata.

articles.title: US uranium production up again
articles.summary: Production of uranium from mines in the USA last year was more than double 2024's figure, and the highest in nine years, according to the latest report of annual data from the Energy Information Administration.

articles.title: Oil and mining giants among firms exploring nuclear's industrial use potential
articles.summary: The Industrial Advanced Nuclear Consortium, whose members include ExxonMobil, Shell, Chevron and Rio Tinto, has published a report outlining the potential for nuclear energy as "a practical, low‐carbon alternative that can be co-located with industrial facilities to provide dependable baseload heat and power, with the grid and renewables servi

articles.title: Blykalla teams up with Hitachi for SMR deployment
articles.summary: Sweden's Blykalla and Hitachi Energy - the energy arm of Japan's Hitachi Group - have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore a long-term collaboration on enabling the deployment of next-generation lead-cooled advanced modular reactors.

articles.title: India inaugurates nuclear-powered hydrogen production facility
articles.summary: The facility uses process heat from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor to produce hydrogen through the copper-chlorine thermochemical process developed by Indian researchers.
